Definition: to hate (as one of an opposite tribe or party); hence to be hostile
BiblicalUsage: God promises Moses that if Israel obeys his voice, he will be an enemy to their enemies and an adversary to their adversaries. The word is hatred between opposite parties — open hostility, not quiet dislike.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this is a promise with a condition: God's enmity toward my enemies follows my obedience to his voice.
